Q: Checking if a graph is connected with Z3 A:

You could check graph connectivity by something like this:

from z3 import *

solver = Solver()

nodes = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"]
Nodes = range(len(nodes))

edges = [ ["A", "B", 5], ["B", "C", 1], ["C", "D", 7], ["D", "A", 9], ["E", "F", 3], ["F", "G", 2], ["G", "E", 3]]

''' every node has a level '''
levels = [Int(f'L{nd}') for nd in Nodes]

''' first node has level 0 '''
solver.add(levels[0] == 0)

''' all nodes != root must have a level one higher than a neighbor node '''
for nd in Nodes:
    if nd > 0:
        ''' collect a set of neighbor nodes connected to node nd '''
        print(f'Node {nd} {nodes[nd]}')
        neighbors = set([nodes.index(x) for x, y, _ in edges if y == nodes[nd]]+[nodes.index(y) for x, y, _ in edges if x == nodes[nd]])
        print(f'neighbors {neighbors}')
        solver.add(Sum([(levels[nd] == (levels[n] + 1)) for n in neighbors]) > 0)

if solver.check() == sat:
    print("Graph is connected")
else:
    print("Graph is not connected")

Q: How to typecheck x.startswith() when x has type str | bytes? A:

If it's at all possible, change your code to stop using str|bytes and instead use a generic TypeVar that must be exactly one of them. You should probably use str|bytes only when you don't care which of the two concrete types any given variable has.

The definition of AnyStr suffices for this purpose. Note that AnyStr itself is deprecated and will be removed from the standard library soon, but you can easily copy its definition into your own code. Note that it is important to use constraints, not bounds, on the TypeVar, since most string manipulation will not preserve types like Literal['foo']

In practice I've found that it is sometimes necessary to refactor out a separate function in some places. Using a nested function rather than a standalone one can help if you have a lot of local variables you want to pass around to differently-typed generic contexts. Note also that mypy is atrociously bad at dealing with loops over different types; sometimes you'll have to manually specify some types and/or unroll some loops manually.

Edit: to demonstrate how this works with the OP's example code, assuming you have an appropate lz4/block.pyi stubs file, the following typechecks:

#!/usr/bin/env python3

import json
from typing_extensions import Any, TypeVar

import lz4.block

AnyStr2 = TypeVar('AnyStr2', str, bytes|bytearray)

bytebuf = bytes|bytearray
MAGIC_HEADER = b"mozLz40\0"

def jsonlz4_loads(buf: AnyStr2) -> Any:
    header: AnyStr2
    if isinstance(buf, bytebuf):
        header = MAGIC_HEADER
    else:
        header = MAGIC_HEADER.decode("ascii")

    if not buf.startswith(header):
        raise ValueError("Not a valid JSONLZ4 buffer - magic bytes missing")

    return json.loads(lz4.block.decompress(buf[len(header):]))

def main() -> None:
    bdata = MAGIC_HEADER + b'\x0f\x00\x00\x00\xf0\x00"hello, world!"'
    print(jsonlz4_loads(bdata))
    print(jsonlz4_loads(bytearray(bdata)))
    # Fails at runtime due to lying documentation.
    print(jsonlz4_loads(bdata.decode('latin1')))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

However, it fails at runtime since the documentation for lz4.block is lying about accepting str (possibly an artifact of the Python2 days?).
